policies.title: Palestinian ordinary passports: 2026 advance-visa visitor cohort
policies.summary: The State of Palestine's current ordinary-passport schedule labels this exact destination cohort "Visa is required" and separately labels electronic and arrival-issued routes elsewhere in the same schedule. It is normalized as advance visa required.
conditions: This is the Ministry's ordinary-passport short-visitor baseline. The source separately labels eVisa and visa-on-arrival rows, so a bare "Visa is required" row is not recast as either route.
Georgia and Panama have separately stated waivers for holders of specified third-country visas. Those conditional document routes are excluded from this passport-only baseline.
Mission availability, passport recognition, individual admission, route, transit, work, residence, diplomatic, official, service and other special-document treatment are outside this policy.

policies.title: Palestinian ordinary passports: Türkiye advance visitor visa
policies.summary: Türkiye's current Foreign Ministry row expressly requires a visa for Palestinian ordinary-passport holders. Its separate eVisa option depends on a qualifying Schengen, United States, United Kingdom or Ireland visa or residence permit, so it does not replace the ordinary passport-only baseline.
conditions: The stated 30-day single-entry eVisa route requires a qualifying third-country visa or residence permit and further conditions; it is excluded from this passport-only baseline.
The policy concerns ordinary short visitor travel only. Work, study, residence, diplomatic and other official or special passports/documents, admission and carrier controls remain separate.

policies.title: Palestinian ordinary passports: 2026 visa-on-arrival visitor cohort
policies.summary: The State of Palestine's current ordinary-passport schedule expressly labels Bangladesh, Comoros and Guinea-Bissau as visa-on-arrival destinations, with stated maximum stays.
conditions: The schedule states up to 30 days for Bangladesh, 45 days for Comoros and 90 days for Guinea-Bissau.

This is an ordinary short-visitor baseline only; availability at a particular port, passport acceptance, onward-travel, health, security, transit, work, residence and final-admission conditions remain separate.

policies.title: Palestinian ordinary passports: 2026 electronic visitor-visa cohort
policies.summary: The State of Palestine's current ordinary-passport schedule expressly labels Burkina Faso, Kyrgyzstan and São Tomé and Príncipe as eVisa destinations.
conditions: This records only the schedule's electronic visitor-visa classification; it does not infer an airport-issued, conditional-document, residence, work, diplomatic, official or special-document route.
Application availability, processing, fees, duration, passport acceptance and final admission remain subject to the destination authority's current procedure.

policies.title: Palestinian ordinary passports: 2026 visa-free visitor cohort
policies.summary: The State of Palestine's current ordinary-passport schedule expressly says no visa is required for short visits to Bolivia and Jordan.
conditions: The schedule states Bolivia is visa-free up to 90 days; it identifies Jordan as no-visa-required without a stated duration.
This is a destination visa classification, not a finding about Israeli-controlled, Egyptian or Jordanian crossing, permit, carrier, security, residence, work or final-admission requirements.

conflicts.officialStatus: unavailable (full visa-issuance suspension for PA-issued or endorsed travel documents)
conflicts.explanation: The State Department fully suspends visa issuance in all nonimmigrant and immigrant categories for travel documents issued or endorsed by the Palestinian Authority, subject to listed exceptions. This cannot be represented as ordinary advance-visa access.
